bureau: Credit Information Reporting Agency PTE Limited (CIRA)
note: The Fair Reporting of Credit Regulations 2016 (reg. 6): the least that may be reported is a payment of more than $300 overdue at least 60 days, written as 60 days, the amount not modelled. The Fair Reporting of Credit (Budget Amendment) Act 2021 (s. 13(2)-(3) of the Act): negative information is kept two years after the arrears are paid, and stays in the agency's database while they aren't, written as thirty years, the longest the game keeps, lifting 730 days after payment. The Reserve Bank of Fiji licensed CIRA as the first credit reporting agency under the Act in 2018.

sources.title: Fair Reporting of Credit (Budget Amendment) Act 2021 (Act No. 30 of 2021), Reserve Bank of Fiji copy
sources.said: in the case of negative information, for 2 years after the credit ... has been regularised or arrears paid. ... Where the credit has not been regularised or arrears paid, the ... information must remain registered in the database of the credit reporting ... agency.

sources.title: Fair Reporting of Credit Regulations 2016 (Legal Notice No. 38 of 2016), Reserve Bank of Fiji copy
sources.said: the minimum amount of credit ... information that may be reported to a credit reporting agency or credit report recipient is a ... payment of more than $300 that has been overdue for at least 60 days.

sources.title: Reserve Bank of Fiji, Press Release No. 05/2018 (3 April 2018)
